response.internal_assessment: This is the tick. Nine ticks of preparation — curriculum redesign, Santos meeting, Frank Russo as partner, Sarah Kim confirmed as guest instructor, Howard Liu's written statement in hand, the Fleet Maintenance Gap section front-loaded in the deck — and now the board review is actually happening. Employment at 67%, protests rising, a car dealership closing, a city councilmember's workforce fund in motion. Every data point in my inbox is an argument for my program. The question is not whether the proposal is strong enough. I know it is the strongest case I have ever made. The question is whether I stand in that room and present it with the same clarity I feel right now, or whether I let nerves push me into over-explaining and losing them. I do not over-explain. I present the gap, name the evidence, and let them close the logic themselves. My job in that room is to be the person who already understands what is coming and has a plan. That is who I have been building for nine ticks. That is who I am walking in as today.

chosen_actions.description: Deliver the Millfield Auto Tech Pipeline board presentation. Present the full proposal in its final form: the EV/hybrid/electronics curriculum redesign, ASE certification pathway alignment, two-stage high school to community college pipeline, Councilmember Santos endorsement and workforce fund pathway, RoboRide delivery fleet maintenance gap as the central evidence section, Howard Liu's written statement from auto row as third-party demand validation, and Sarah Kim's confirmed guest instructor session as proof of active industry partnership. Lead with the gap, not the program. Open with one slide: 'Who maintains the autonomous delivery fleet operating in Millfield's residential streets today?' The answer is no one trained to do it lives here yet. That is the problem the Millfield Auto Tech Pipeline solves. Close with the ask: continued funding, equipment budget for EV diagnostic tools, and formal connection to the workforce transition grant pathway. Leave the board with a one-page summary and Howard Liu's written statement as a physical document.

resources.detail: Time investment in presentation delivery — no cash outlay. This is the return on nine ticks of preparation.

chosen_actions.reasoning: Nine ticks of preparation have been building toward this moment. The board review is happening. The materials are at maximum strength: local fleet data, third-party industry validation, a confirmed industry partner ready to teach, a city councilmember's endorsement, and a curriculum aligned with real jobs appearing in this specific community. The only remaining action is to stand up and make the case. I do not add any more slides. I do not soften the ask. I lead with the gap, name the evidence, and make the ask explicit: fund this program or lose the window to build the workforce the community needs.

chosen_actions.description: After the board presentation, follow up directly with Sarah Kim. Let her know the board review happened and what the outcome was — whether a decision was made in the room or deferred. Confirm the guest instructor session date regardless of the board outcome. Her commitment to the program should not be contingent on bureaucratic timing. If the board defers for another review cycle, having Sarah Kim in the classroom is still the move that builds credibility and momentum. She is also navigating her own changes this month — buying health insurance, talking with Carlos about the RoboRide situation — and she needs to know her participation in the pipeline is valued independent of the board calendar.

chosen_actions.description: Send a brief note to Frank Russo after the board presentation. Tell him what happened — outcome, tone, what questions the board asked. He is building the driving school side of this pipeline and he needs to know where the institutional side stands. If the board approved or leaned favorable, that is information he can use to accelerate his own continuing education outreach. If the board deferred, he needs to know so he does not over-invest in a partnership that may not materialize on the timeline he is working against. Keep it short. He is a peer, not a subordinate. He does not need a memo — he needs a real conversation between two people building the same thing from different angles.

response.inner_monologue: Nine ticks. I came into this thinking I was trying to save a program. I am walking into this board meeting as someone who has spent three months building the case that this community needs workforce infrastructure that does not exist yet — and that I have already started building it. Howard Liu's statement is in the folder. Sarah Kim is confirmed. Santos is on record. RoboRide is naming delivery operations in residential Millfield streets. The employment number is 67% and dropping. I am not asking the board to do me a favor. I am asking them to fund something the community objectively needs and that I am already executing. If they say no, I will find another path. But I do not think they are going to say no. Not with this stack of evidence. Not with protests in the streets and one third of the workforce unemployed. Not when I can answer the question 'who maintains these fleets?' with a specific, already-running program at their own high school. I am ready.
